Grambsch-Therneau Test of Proportional Hazards

Source: R/test_proportional_hazards.R
test_proportional_hazards.Rd

For each treatment arm other than the control arm (the first level of ARM), fits a Cox model to the data of the two arms and tests the proportional hazards assumption with the score test of Grambsch and Therneau (1994) as implemented in survival::cox.zph().

Usage

test_proportional_hazards(data, transform = c("km", "rank", "identity", "log"))

Arguments

data

Data frame returned by processing_dataset, with two or more treatment arms.

transform

Transformation of time for the test: "km" (the default of survival::cox.zph()), "rank", "identity" or "log".

Value

A data frame with the columns comparison, log_hr (Cox estimate of the log hazard ratio), chisq, df and p_value.

References

Grambsch PM, Therneau TM (1994). Proportional hazards tests and diagnostics based on weighted residuals. Biometrika 81(3):515-526. doi:10.1093/biomet/81.3.515

Examples

raw <- generate_dummy_survival_data(
  arm = c("Control", "Treatment"), n = c(100, 100),
  hazards = log(2) / c(12, 18), dropout_per_year = 0.1, seed = 123
)
dat <- processing_dataset(raw, column_arm = "ARM",
                          column_survtime = "SURVTIME",
                          column_cnsr = "CNSR", control_arm = "Control")
test_proportional_hazards(dat)
#>             comparison     log_hr     chisq df   p_value
#> 1 Treatment vs Control -0.3793755 0.0198715  1 0.8878966
